author: The Current
description:
Brother Wallace recalls meeting Peter Gabriel at the studio Gabriel owns
Support The Current: https://support.mpr.org/youtube or hit the Thanks button

Georgia singer-songwriter Brother Wallaces releases his debut album, "Electric Love," on May 8, 2026, on @atorecords. The album was recorded at Real World Studios near Bath, England. The facility is owned by musician Peter Gabriel.

During a live performance in the Forum at Minnesota Public Radio, Brother Wallace tells The Current's Bill DeVille about what it was like to record at Real World Studios, and how he got to meet Peter Gabriel while there.

Watch the full set here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eDom_4T2KWY

description:
Alsa Bruno of Brass Solidarity on navigating community grief with music.

Brass Solidarity was formed as a response to George Floyd’s murder in 2020 with a mission to heal through music in community.

You can catch the band at George Floyd Square every Monday 5:30-7pm and at MinneHONK Festival this weekend.

Find more information at minnehonk.org
title: Brass Solidarity on navigating community grief with music #BrassSolidarity

author: The Current
description:
Drummer Bailey Minzenberger describes how Friko embrace dynamics
Support The Current: https://support.mpr.org/youtube or hit the Thanks button

Chicago band Friko recently visited The Current to talk to host Zach McCormick about their new album, "Something Worth Waiting For," which released April 24, 2026, on @atorecords.

During the interview, Zach notes the band lean into dynamics in their song arrangements. Friko drummer Bailey Minzenberger talks about the band's fondness for the quiet and loud moments in music. "Leaning into dynamics is something that we've always really loved," Minzenberger says. "And I think to an extent comes kind of naturally because it's the way that we play."

title: Friko talk about leaning into dynamics on song arrangements

author: The Current
description:
Watch Brother Wallace and his band perform "Who's That?" live
Support The Current: https://support.mpr.org/youtube or hit the Thanks button

Georgia singer-songwriter Chris Wallace — known artistically as Brother Wallace — has been a choir director and music teacher, but his musical acumen led him to a connection and collaboration with U.K. band The Heavy. It was from that friendship that Brother Wallace's career as a soul and R&B artist got underway. "You got one life," Wallace says. "You might as well live it to the fullest."

Brother Wallace's debut album, Electric Love, releases on May 8, 2026, on ATO Records. Now touring in support of the album, Brother Wallace and his band visited the Forum at Minnesota Public Radio to play a live set before a studio audience. Between songs, Brother Wallace chatted with The Current's Bill DeVille about his life and career so far. Watch the full session above. 

Musicians

title: Brother Wallace — Who's That? (live at the Forum at Minnesota Public Radio)
